summary: This survey presents a full-stack view of quantum compiler design for fault-tolerant quantum error correction, organizing compiler techniques into three interacting layers: logical-level QEC compilation, physical-level QEC realization, and decoder runtime integration. The work reviews surface-code lattice-surgery compilers, beyond-surface-code and qLDPC code-surgery frameworks, syndrome-extraction scheduling, hardware-aware implementation on superconducting/trapped-ion/neutral-atom platforms, and real-time decoding algorithms including matching, belief propagation, and neural approaches.
motivation: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computation requires moving beyond circuit optimization toward encoding-aware, protocol-structured compilation that jointly optimizes algorithmic operations, logical error correction procedures, hardware constraints, and classical decoding. Recent experimental demonstrations of below-threshold surface-code memories and logical processors have made QEC-aware compilation an urgent systems problem.
method: The survey organizes existing work into three coupled compiler layers: (1) logical level—where algorithmic gates are lowered into lattice-surgery operations, magic-state distillation, and code switching; (2) physical level—where syndrome circuits are scheduled and mapped to superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom hardware under connectivity and timing constraints; (3) runtime—where detector error models are generated and decoded in real time using matching, belief propagation, or neural algorithms.
result: The survey identifies key cross-layer bottlenecks: layouts optimized for routing can strain decoders, hardware-friendly schedules can waste magic-state resources, and codes with favorable asymptotic parameters may incur unacceptable overhead once mapping and decoding costs are included. Open challenges include compiler-decoder co-design, qLDPC operation synthesis, resource-flow management for magic states, and end-to-end benchmarking across all three layers on shared evaluation baselines.
